findings.issue: No existing e2e spec in the repo presses Tab, so Alt+Tab for WebKit has no repo precedent. It is the usual Playwright workaround for macOS WebKit, where Tab skips buttons unless Full Keyboard Access is on. On macOS, Alt flips that setting, so on a Mac with Full Keyboard Access turned on, Alt+Tab would skip the buttons and the test would fail. CI is Linux WebKit (ubuntu-24.04), where Tab reaches buttons and Alt does not stop focus moving. The comment presents a macOS-only behaviour as if it were true of WebKit everywhere.
findings.evidence: grep for press('Tab') / Alt+Tab in e2e/ and tests/ finds only this file. The repo's existing per-browser convention is test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', reason), e.g. e2e/responsive-table.spec.ts:87 and e2e/rapid-pace.spec.ts:280. The local run of the spec (macOS) passed 6 of 6. The CI run 45629763982 was still in progress when this review was written.
findings.fix: Either reword the comment to say this is the macOS WebKit keyboard-access workaround, or pick the key from the platform (process.platform === 'darwin' && browserName === 'webkit' ? 'Alt+Tab' : 'Tab'). Then confirm the WebKit run in CI is green.

summary: The change matches the spec. openStatistics() in App.tsx is now the only reset path: Home's onStatistics and the report's onStatistics both point to it, and the Screen union is unchanged. There is no race with the session-end write. The report only renders after endSession resolves (App.tsx:132-146), and the stats effect reads trendData() after tableWritesSettled(). The e2e asserts '51 hands over 2 sessions', which proves the session that just ended is counted. The Back to Home markup is byte-identical to before; only its parent div is new. No locked test file is touched, and all five locked report Vitest files pass. Focus is unchanged: the report heading is focused. DOM and Tab order are View statistics, then Back to Home, and the e2e checks both. The new Vitest file (2 tests) and the e2e spec (3 tests x Chromium and WebKit) both pass locally. Scope is 313 lines against a budget of 230. About 53 lines are product code, CSS and docs. About 260 are the two new test files the spec requires: three e2e scenarios with shared setup, plus locally declared locators, which is how the other e2e specs in the repo do it. The overrun is justified. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings, only 2 MINOR and 1 NIT. The WebKit Alt+Tab choice has no repo precedent, and its comment describes macOS-only behaviour. CI on the branch was still running when this review was written.
